subject: Proposal: exit-conditioning + 60-day notice option for ACME order form
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 7 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: exit-conditioning + 60-day notice option for ACME order form

Hi team,

ACME legal came back on term/renewal and wants tighter exit rights across the MSA/order form. They specifically pushed for a 30-day auto-renew opt-out and a broad termination-for-convenience (T4C) right on the Order Form.

My stance: we can be flexible on notice windows but need to keep T4C scoped (order-form level only) and protect Hosted/Dedicated capacity commitments (so we avoid running up costs from churn). Proposed trade: allow a 60-day opt-out window (instead of our standard 90) for enterprise order forms if ACME commits to a 3-month reserved capacity guarantee or a pro-rated ramp credit.

Attachments: ACME_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (redline with our suggested language) and Mutual-Exit-Matrix.xlsx (shows financial impact modeling for different notice windows).

Asks:
- Laura: quick legal review of the redline language (see attached). Focus on T4C carve-outs, notice periods, and the interplay with auto-renew.
- Markus/Karthik: confirm whether a 3-month commit discount (or credit) is acceptable commercially as the trade for 60 days.

Goal: get back to ACME with a single-option compromise this week.

Thanks,
Monica
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 7 Nov 2026 10:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: exit-conditioning + 60-day notice option for ACME order form

Monica / team —

Thanks for the context and the redline. High-level legal summary after a quick pass:

- Auto-renew: Accept 60-day opt-out language for enterprise order forms only. Need explicit callout that notice must be provided per order form (not at service-level) so we can tombstone KV caches and drain capacity.
- Termination for Convenience (T4C): We should push to limit T4C to non-production or pilot order forms, or to order forms where the customer has not consumed > X% of committed capacity. Broad T4C at enterprise scale creates significant stranded-cost risk.
- Refunds and ramp credits: Recommend prorated refund for unused pre-paid amounts and a 30-day wind-down support obligation. Avoid open-ended transition obligations.
- Definition clarity: Make sure "Termination Date", "Notice Window", and "Order Form" are defined consistently across MSA and OF.

I've attached a version with suggested edits inline (ACME_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf). The Mutual-Exit-Matrix quantifies the worst-case impact under T4C; bookmark the sheet labeled "60d_vs_30d".

If commercial is comfortable offering a 3-month commit in exchange for the 60-day notice, legal is comfortable signing off on scoped T4C language with the refund/proration and a limited transition support obligation.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

From: Sam Li <samantha.li@acme-prod.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Legal <legal@acme-prod.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2026 11:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: exit-conditioning + 60-day notice option for ACME order form

Monica —

Thanks for the redline. A couple of points from ACME Legal / procurement:

1) Notice window: ACME prefers a 30-day opt-out across the board, but we can consider longer windows for production rolls if Redwood can demonstrate a material benefit.
2) T4C: ACME wants symmetrical termination for convenience at the order form level without carve-outs — our legal lead says it's standard for us to be able to exit commitments with business reasons.
3) Refunds: we expect a pro-rata refund for unused pre-paid amounts.

We understand your capacity/cost concerns. Could we propose a tiered approach: 30-day for pilots and non-prod order forms; 60-day for production/enterprise; and mutual T4C with a fee schedule for early exits on enterprise orders? That would allow us to scale confidently while giving Redwood some predictability.

Open to a call tomorrow afternoon to resolve if you prefer.

— Sam
Samantha Li, Senior Procurement Manager | ACME Productivity
samantha.li@acme-prod.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Li <samantha.li@acme-prod.com>
Cc: ACME Legal <legal@acme-prod.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: exit-conditioning + 60-day notice option for ACME order form

Sam —

Appreciate the constructive suggestion. The tiered approach is workable and aligns with our risk model. Here's a concise compromise proposal for redline: 

- Pilots / non-production order forms: 30-day opt-out, mutual T4C allowed, full pro-rated refund for unused pre-paid amounts.
- Production / enterprise order forms: 60-day opt-out; T4C allowed only if the customer pays a termination fee equal to the prorated value of reserved capacity for the remainder of the committed period OR accepts a 30% early-termination service charge (whichever is higher).
- All refunds to be prorated; Redwood provides 30 days of transition support by default, additional support on SOW.

Commercial ask: in exchange for the stricter protection on production orders, Redwood will offer ACME a 10% credit on the first 3 months of reserved capacity if ACME signs a minimum 3-month committed capacity addendum on the first production order.

Laura has flagged the legal language we need to capture these mechanics. Markus/Karthik — can you confirm approval for the 10%/3-month commercial concession? If yes, I'll send a clean redline back to ACME today and offer a quick call if they want to walk through the matrix.

Thanks,
Monica
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: exit-conditioning + 60-day notice option for ACME order form

Monica / team —

Approved. 10% credit on first 3 months in exchange for a 3-month minimum reserved commit is acceptable for a strategic enterprise account like ACME. Also okay with the tiered notice approach and the capped termination charge for production orders as long as legal finalizes the language to protect our committed pools.

Proceed to send the revised redline to Sam and ACME Legal. If they push back on the 3-month commit, come back to me with the financial delta; we can consider a smaller credit or a time-limited pilot concession.

Markus Klein
VP Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
